name: Digital-Nomad-Research
what_it_holds: Academic replication package for digital-nomad-visa policy adoption. Processed dataset DigitalNomadDataset.xlsx with two sheets: tourism_and_macroeconomic_data (2,464 country-year rows: GDP, unemployment, tourism expenditure and GDP share, tourism employment, business/total tourism arrivals, internet usage, inflation, FX rate, price-level index) and policy_data (33 confirmed digital-nomad-visa adopter countries: adoption timing, permit duration, income requirements, visa fees, tax treatment, remote-work eligibility). Also ships intermediate LLM-audit files (LLM_Stage1.xlsx, LLM_Stage2.xlsx, Audit_Stage1_Stage2.csv) documenting a 190-jurisdiction screening process. Applies TWFE and a Callaway-Sant'Anna-style group-time DID estimator to the policy adoption. MIT license (code); underlying World Bank/UN Tourism data retain their own licences. Last substantive update 2026-08-09.
why_useful: Directly fills gap 16 (digital-nomad visa dataset) with a genuine policy panel plus a much broader 190-country tourism/macro panel that could substitute or cross-check for LatAm/APAC travel-volume gaps (gap 7).
time_coverage: multi-year panel (years not fully specified in README summary)
size_hint: one xlsx, 2,464 rows in macro panel + 33 policy records
license: MIT (code); third-party data retains original licence

Directly addresses gap 16 (remote-work/long-stay demand, digital-nomad visa datasets) with an actual policy-adoption panel and a country-year tourism/macro panel across 190 countries -- usable to test whether digital-nomad-visa adoption correlates with long-stay booking demand in ABNB's addressable markets, and the event-study/DID method itself is reusable for other ABNB-adjacent policy shocks (e.g. STR ordinances).

Directly targets gap #16 (remote-work/long-stay demand) with a pre-built causal-inference template (Callaway-Sant'Anna) we already use elsewhere in the repo (margin/regulatory work) — visa-adoption events are testable against Airbnb's long-stay night share by region.

name: MarkPhamm/local_warehouse_pipeline
what_it_holds: A local-first ELT pipeline (dlt + PyArrow extraction, DuckDB + dbt transform, Prefect orchestration, Visivo dashboards) that pulls CFPB consumer-complaint data live from the CFPB complaints API. Users configure target companies and start dates in src/cfg/config.py; staged data lands as daily Parquet files under landing/cfpb_complaints/YYYY_MM_DD/, one file per company per day, supporting incremental and historical backfills. MIT-licensed, updated 27 Jun 2026, 11 stars.
why_useful: A ready-made, working, non-Airbnb-site method to pull CFPB complaint records filtered to a target company — pointed at 'Airbnb, Inc.' as the configured company this becomes exactly the sanctioned CFPB-complaints-about-Airbnb dataset the theme asks for (refund/cancellation complaint counts and text as a service-friction proxy), without scraping airbnb.com itself.
time_coverage: configurable start date to present, daily granularity
size_hint: pipeline code, not a static dataset; output scales with configured pull window
themes: Consumer credit and BNPL: Klarna/Affirm public stats, Fed G.19, credit card delinquency, CFPB complaints dataset (Airbnb refund complaints), BBB complaint scrapers
why_all: A ready-made, working, non-Airbnb-site method to pull CFPB complaint records filtered to a target company — pointed at 'Airbnb, Inc.' as the configured company this becomes exactly the sanctioned CFPB-complaints-about-Airbnb dataset the theme asks for (refund/cancellation complaint counts and text as a service-friction proxy), without scraping airbnb.com itself.

name: nowcasting-mexico
what_it_holds: Reproducible Snakemake pipeline nowcasting Mexican IGAE (economic-activity index) 2018-2024 using Banxico API series (exchange rate, CETES, M1, credit), INEGI flat files (industrial production, retail sales, unemployment), Google Trends (7 keywords) and Google Mobility (2020-2022). Implements AR(4), MIDAS, DFM, LASSO, Ridge, Random Forest with pseudo-out-of-sample evaluation, R+Python, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20563443 for the writeup. No committed data files, but automated pull scripts for all sources.
why_useful: Directly answers gap #17 (nowcasting with mixed-frequency data, MIDAS/DFM) applied to Mexican macro activity, which is a LatAm demand proxy for ABNB's Mexico City market; the code pattern (Banxico pull + Trends + mobility + MIDAS) is reusable for a Mexico travel-demand nowcast.
time_coverage: not stated in listing, IGAE monthly series
themes: Regional macro for LatAm and APAC: Mexico INEGI/Banxico, Brazil IBGE/BCB, Argentina INDEC, Colombia DANE, Chile, Japan e-Stat, Korea KOSIS, Australia ABS, India MOSPI clients
Google Trends tooling and datasets: pytrends, gtab anchored trends, historical trends archives, trends nowcasting repos
Nowcasting methods and packages: MIDAS, dynamic factor models, bridge equations, nowcasting with Google Trends, KPI nowcasting for companies
why_all: Directly answers gap #17 (nowcasting with mixed-frequency data, MIDAS/DFM) applied to Mexican macro activity, which is a LatAm demand proxy for ABNB's Mexico City market; the code pattern (Banxico pull + Trends + mobility + MIDAS) is reusable for a Mexico travel-demand nowcast.

Fills gap #7 (LatAm regional travel/economic volume — Mexico specifically) via a live Banxico API client plus a full MIDAS/DFM nowcasting toolkit (also relevant to gap #17's 'nowcasting with mixed-frequency data' ask), reusable as a template even if the Google Trends leg alone is weak.

Direct template for gap #7 (LatAm regional travel/consumer volume, esp. Mexico DATATUR/INEGI-adjacent) and gap #17 (mixed-frequency nowcasting methods incl. MIDAS/DFM combined with Google Trends and mobility data) — could be adapted to nowcast ABNB LatAm nights using Mexico macro + Trends + mobility as regressors, and the MIDAS/DFM code is directly reusable methodology.

name: openstates-scrapers
what_it_holds: Open States project's scraper codebase (22,236 commits, GPL-3.0, actively maintained) covering bills and votes for all 50 US state legislatures, feeding the Open States API/bulk data. Not itself a committed bill-text dataset here, but the live method to pull every state-level short-term-rental bill (registration caps, tax changes, statewide preemption fights) with bill status history.
why_useful: A much larger and more actively maintained alternative to pylegiscan for a US state-level STR-ordinance/bill tracker (gap #12): openstates.org's own bulk data/API (not scraped by us) could be queried for 'short-term rental' bills across all 50 states with full text and status history.
last_activity: very active, 22,236 commits total on repo
time_coverage: varies by state, generally multi-year current-session coverage via openstates.org bulk data
size_hint: large scraper codebase; actual bill data lives on openstates.org, not committed in this repo
themes: News and event databases: GDELT tooling, Google News scrapers, travel-industry news datasets (Skift, PhocusWire), regulatory news trackers
STR regulation trackers and ordinance datasets: city STR law databases, Legistar/LegiScan clients, EU parliament open data, court records (CourtListener/RECAP) on Airbnb litigation
why_all: A much larger and more actively maintained alternative to pylegiscan for a US state-level STR-ordinance/bill tracker (gap #12): openstates.org's own bulk data/API (not scraped by us) could be queried for 'short-term rental' bills across all 50 states with full text and status history.

Fills gap #12 (STR ordinance/legislation trackers) at the state level across all 50 states, complementing city-level Legistar coverage; state preemption laws are a first-order driver of city STR caps that affect Airbnb US supply.
